SARB BOP Codes 2026: Full List, Property Codes and Remittance Steps

2026.08.03 · Updated 2026.10.16 14 min read Scott Huang Tax & Regulation

BOP codes are the two-part numbers — a three-digit category plus a two-digit sub-category — that South Africa's exchange-control system uses to classify every cross-border payment. If you are a non-resident buying Cape Town property, your inward payment is reported under 510 01: Investment or disinvestment of property by a non-resident individual. A wrong or missing code is the most common reason a transfer is held or flagged, so the table below lists the codes buyers actually need, then walks through the remittance steps.

Immigration and tax experts at Foreign Buyer Property Solutions (FBPS) note that the new code system encompasses over 800 categories and subcategories, a level of granularity far exceeding the previous framework. For Taiwanese investors considering or already holding property in Cape Town, understanding these new rules is essential for ensuring the safe movement of capital across borders.

Key Insight: The SARB's BoP code update is not a routine administrative adjustment — it is a structural reform aligning South Africa with the IMF's Balance of Payments Manual (Version 6). For foreign property investors, the correct BoP classification is the passport for capital to flow freely; an incorrect classification can become a roadblock. Now that the harmonised list has been in force since 11 August 2026, the priority has shifted from reading the new rules to auditing the codes already attached to your transactions — particularly the inward code recorded when your capital first entered the country.

Which SARB BOP Codes Apply to Foreign Property Buyers? The 2026 Reference Table

Direct answer: A BOP code (also written BoP, for Balance of Payments) is the category your bank — an authorised dealer — must report to the South African Reserve Bank for every cross-border payment, inward or outward. It is written as a three-digit category plus a two-digit sub-code, so 103 01 is category 103, sub-code 01. For a foreign buyer, four entries carry almost all the weight: 510 01 when an individual brings capital in to buy South African property, 503 when a company or trust does the same, and the same two codes in reverse when the property is sold and the proceeds are repatriated.

Your transaction Direction BOP code How SARB names the category
Non-resident individual brings capital in to buy South African property Inward 510 01 Investment into property by a non-resident individual
Non-resident company or trust invests into South African property Inward 503 Investment into property by a non-resident corporate entity
Non-resident individual sells the property and repatriates the proceeds Outward 510 01 Disinvestment of property by a non-resident individual
Non-resident company sells the property and repatriates the proceeds Outward 503 Disinvestment of property by a non-resident corporate entity
Buying goods from an overseas supplier (import payment) Outward 103 01 Import payment — sub-codes 02–11 isolate capital goods, gold, platinum, crude oil, refined petroleum products, gemstones, steel, coal, iron ore and post
Receiving money for goods sold abroad (export proceeds) Inward 103 01 Export proceeds — same sub-code structure as the import side
Paying a supplier before the goods ship Outward 101 01 / 102 01 / 104 01 Import advance payment (the 102 and 104 variants apply where an import undertaking is in place)
Goods change hands but nothing physically ships either way Inward or Outward 109 + commodity sub-code Proceeds for / payments for goods where no physical export or import will take place
Salary received from an overseas employer Inward 304 Remuneration paid by a non-resident to a resident employee (excluding remittances)
Salary paid to a non-resident employee Outward 304 Remuneration paid by a resident to a non-resident employee (excluding remittances)
Migrant or foreign contract worker remittances Inward or Outward 416 / 417 Migrant worker remittances / foreign national contract worker remittances (excluding compensation)
Rent collected on a South African property Inward 308 Rental
Tuition for a child studying in Cape Town Inward 254 · Outward 285 254 / 285 Travel services for non-residents – education travel / tuition fees
Purchase of land, mineral rights, leases, licences or goodwill Outward 505 Purchase of land, mineral rights, forestry rights, contracts, leases, licenses, goodwill and similar rights
Emigrating and taking fixed property out of South Africa Outward 530 01 Emigration foreign capital allowance – fixed property

The rule that actually catches people out: the code is not a one-off box you tick at entry. The outward code used when you sell has to reconcile with the inward code recorded when you bought. If the two do not tell the same story, the bank suspends the transfer and refers it to the Financial Surveillance Department — and that referral, not the tax bill, is where "frozen capital" usually comes from.

Sources: SARB FinSurv Reporting System Operations Manual, Section B.3 (Balance of Payments categories, inward and outward); the harmonised SARB BoP category list in force from 11 August 2026 as published by Nedbank and RMB Private Bank. Codes are reproduced for orientation only — the authorised dealer makes the final classification, so confirm the code with your bank before you instruct an international transfer.

What Is a BOP Code and Why Must Foreign Buyers Care?

Direct answer: If the phrase you searched for was simply what is BOP code, this is the one-sentence version: it is the label your bank files with the Reserve Bank to say what a cross-border payment was for. More precisely, a BOP code is the classification your bank attaches to a cross-border payment — a category number plus a sub-code, such as 103 01 for a goods payment or 510 01 for a non-resident individual investing in South African property. It states the purpose of the money, and it is what later allows that money to leave again.

If the phrase you actually searched for is a BOP code South Africa list, the first thing to know is that the Reserve Bank schedule runs to hundreds of lines while a foreign buyer of Cape Town property only ever needs the capital-transfer group. For an individual that is 510 01 on the way in, and the same code on the way out when the property is sold and the proceeds are repatriated. Goods, services, salaries and royalties in the same schedule belong to different transactions and must not be attached to the property payment — mixing them is the compliance error that delays a repatriation years later.

South Africa remains an exchange control jurisdiction where cross-border capital movements are closely regulated. The BoP reporting system is the electronic messaging system that authorised dealers (commercial banks) use to report cross-border transactions to the SARB. When a foreign buyer brings funds into South Africa to purchase property, the bank uses a specific forex BoP code — also described as a foreign exchange BoP code — to declare the nature of the transaction to the SARB. If you have ever searched for which forex BoP code to use in South Africa, the answer depends entirely on how the property is held and what the funds are for.

This code is not a simple checkbox — it declares the nature of the funds to the SARB, and the classification depends on the type of investment structure and what the property will be used for. The correct BoP classification will enable you to transfer your proceeds abroad when exiting the South African property market, while an incorrect code can result in delays or even freezing of your capital.

The framework covers both inward transactions and outward flows. Inward transactions BoP codes govern how capital arriving from Taiwan is declared when it is used to buy Cape Town property, while the outward codes govern repatriation at exit. Getting the inward declaration right at the start is what makes a clean exit possible later.

Lightstone data shows (Source: Lightstone Foreign Buyer Report, 2026) that foreign buyers now account for approximately 40% of South African home sales above R20 million. Paul Stevens, CEO of Just Property, notes that international buyers are no longer looking at South African luxury homes only as investments, but as places to live, work remotely, holiday and return to. As foreign buyer participation grows, BoP reporting compliance becomes increasingly critical.

What Are the SARB Personal BOP Codes for Foreign Investment?

Direct answer: For an individual moving personal capital to buy South African immovable property, the relevant category is 510 01 — "Investment into property by a non-resident individual". If the purchase is made through a company or a trust instead, the category becomes 503 — "Investment into property by a non-resident corporate entity". The property codes sit in group E (transfers of a capital nature), which is why they are not interchangeable with a payment for goods or services.

This section exists because SARB personal BOP codes foreign investment is one of the most common phrasings buyers search for — and because the answer is narrower than most of them expect.

Which forex BOP code should you use in South Africa?

Use the code that matches the purpose of the funds, not the channel they arrive through. A wire transfer, a SWIFT payment and a debit from an offshore account all report identically — the code describes what the money is for. For a purchase of Cape Town property funded with your own offshore savings, that purpose is a capital investment in immovable property, so 510 01 applies to the individual and 503 to a corporate or trust holder. Common mis-filings are classifying the purchase as a loan from a related party, or filing under a generic "not allocated" category because the funds arrived in tranches.

Does a company or trust use a different code from an individual?

Yes, and the distinction survives the sale. A non-resident individual exits under 510 01 ("Disinvestment of property by a non-resident individual"); a non-resident corporate entity exits under 503. Where a South African resident company invests into property in its own name, the outgoing category is 504 — a different code again, because the investor is a resident rather than a non-resident. If the structure is a DingYao lawyer trust protection arrangement, the trust itself is the reporting entity, so the corporate category is the one that applies. Getting the entity question right at entry is what keeps the exit clean.

Which BoP Code Matches Your Transaction? Nine Situations Mapped

Direct answer: the BoP code follows the nature of the money, not the bank, the currency or the direction on its own. Find the block below, then let your Authorised Dealer confirm the exact sub-code — you are the one who has to justify the code that ends up on the declaration.

Situation you are reportingCategory to reportWhat decides it
Sale of goods (import or export)103 01 where the goods have shipped; 101 for advance payment or advance proceeds; 109 01 where goods are bought or sold with no physical export or import; 110 00 for merchantingWhether the goods physically moved, and whether the money moved before or after shipment — not the value of the shipment
Salary paid into a Standard Bank account304 00 — remuneration paid by a non-resident to a resident employee; 303 00 where the employee is temporarily abroad, 305 00/306 00 for migrant and contract workers; 416 00/417 00 where the money is a remittance rather than remunerationThe nature of the earnings. The bank holding the account does not change the category — a salary credited to a Standard Bank account is reported under the same code as one credited anywhere else in South Africa
Studying (tuition and living costs)285 01 tuition fees attended in person, 285 02 attended online where a resident pays a foreign institution; 258 00 education travel for living costs abroad; 254 and 294 00 where a non-resident studies in South Africa (inward education travel and education service proceeds)Direction decides the pair: a resident studying abroad reports 285/258, a non-resident studying in South Africa reports 254/294
Trust distribution315 00 resident trust income distribution to a non-resident trust; 540 00 resident trust capital distribution to a non-resident trust; 530 07 emigration capital distribution from trustsWhether the distribution is income or capital, and whether it arises from emigration
Inward transactions (money arriving in South Africa)There is no single "inward" code. Inward payments are grouped A to F — merchandise 101/103/109/110, services 2xx, income on financial assets 3xx, current transfers 4xx, capital transfers 5xx, loans and miscellaneous payments 8xxDirection only tells you which half of the schedule to read; the nature of the funds picks the category
Which forex BoP code applies at allDecide in three steps: direction (inward or outward) → nature (goods, services, income, current transfer, capital transfer, loan) → sub-code (commodity or instrument)The sub-code narrows within a category; it never overrides the category. Where two categories look plausible, the declaration trail decides — not the label you would prefer
SARB personal BoP codes for an individual285 tuition, 304 salary, 313 00/314 00/315 00 investment income, prizes and trust income, 401 00/409 00/410 gifts, inheritances and maintenance, 510/511/513 capital, 416 00/417 00 remittancesIndividual codes sit inside the same A to F schedule as corporate ones — "personal" describes the holder, not a separate list
Sending money to yourself (own funds across the border)No self-transfer code exists. Report by the nature of the funds: 510 02 disinvestment of your own capital as a non-resident individual, 313 00 income on your own individual investment, 511/512/513 where a resident individual is investing abroadOwnership does not change the code. The bank still needs the trail showing the funds are yours and where they came from
"BoP code South Africa" — where the list itself livesThe SARB FinSurv category schedule, Sections A to F in both directions, in force from 11 August 2026 (more than 800 categories and sub-categories)Any code list circulating online that predates 11 August 2026 is the previous framework — check the version before you quote a number

Sources: SARB FinSurv Reporting System Operations Manual, Section B.3 — BoP categories (inward and outward payments); harmonised SARB BoP category list in force 11 August 2026, Nedbank guide version 20260806/v006. The category number describes the transaction; the Authorised Dealer enters the final code.

What Changed in the 2026 Upgrade to 800+ BoP Categories?

The updated BoP code framework aligns with the IMF's Balance of Payments Manual (Version 6 or BPM6) (Source: IMF BPM6 Framework). It is intended to standardise category code structures, descriptions, direction rules, and supporting information requirements for transactions across borders. FNB noted in a client communication (Source: FNB Property Barometer, 2026 Q2) that the harmonised requirements apply to both inward and outward transactions, including import and export payments, advance payments and receipts, and other cross-border payments requiring BoP reporting.

Item Old System New System (from 11 Aug 2026)
Number of categories ~200+ categories 800+ categories and subcategories
International standard Partial BPM5 alignment Full BPM6 alignment
Reporting scope Primarily large transactions All cross-border transactions, regardless of amount
Processing efficiency Higher manual review ratio Straight-through processing (STP) in CMA
SARS consistency No mandatory requirement Must match tax disclosure

According to FNB, the harmonised structure is aimed at improving reporting accuracy, ensuring consistent BoP classification, and enhancing the quality of data used by the SARB for economic analysis, financial stability monitoring, and policy formulation. It should also improve straight-through processing of payments within the Common Monetary Area (CMA), making qualifying transactions more efficient.

What BOP Code Do You Use for Goods, Salary and Other Non-Property Flows?

Direct answer: Property is only one of several reasons a foreign buyer moves money. Furniture and fittings shipped to Cape Town report under the goods categories (101/102/103/104 for physical shipments, 109 where nothing physically moves); a salary reports under 304; and each of these is a different declaration from the property investment. Filing them together is the single most common compliance error in this area.

What is the BOP code for sale of goods?

For a sale of goods across the border, the code depends on which way the goods and the money travel and on what is in the shipment. Physical imports are reported under 103 ("Import payment") when the goods have shipped, 101, 102 or 104 when you are paying in advance, and the two-digit sub-code then isolates the commodity — 01 for general goods, 02 for capital goods, 03 gold, 04 platinum, 05 crude oil, 06 refined petroleum products, 07 gemstones, 08 steel, 09 coal, 10 iron ore, 11 post. Exports are reported under the matching 103 export-proceeds category. Where goods are bought or sold and no physical export or import takes place at all — a frequent pattern for equipment sourced inside South Africa for a Cape Town property — the category is 109 with the commodity sub-code, and 110 is reserved for merchanting transactions where you buy and resell without the goods entering the country.

What is the BOP code for a salary paid into a Standard Bank account?

Salaries are reported under category 304 — "Remuneration paid by a non-resident to a resident employee" where the payer sits outside South Africa, and the mirror entry 304 covers a resident employer paying a non-resident employee. Adjacent codes matter here: 303 covers a resident employee temporarily abroad, 305 a migrant worker, and 306 a foreign national contract worker. Plain remittances — money sent home rather than paid as compensation — sit under 416 (migrant worker remittances) and 417 (foreign national contract worker remittances). Whichever South African bank processes the credit, including Standard Bank, the BOP code for salary payments describes the nature of the earnings rather than the account they land in — a salary credited to a Standard Bank account is reported under exactly the same category as one credited anywhere else in South Africa.

Which BoP Code Applies to Your Cape Town Property Scenario?

For Taiwanese investors purchasing property in Cape Town, the choice of BoP code depends on several factors. Here are the four most common investment structures and their corresponding BoP reporting considerations:

Individual Ownership

Foreign buyer purchases property in personal name. Funds are reported as "personal capital transfers." Simplest structure, but requires attention to estate planning and tax residency status.

Company Ownership

Property held through a South African or offshore company. Funds reported as "direct investment" or "portfolio investment" depending on the corporate structure. Company registration documents must align with BoP reporting.

Trust Structure

Property held through a lawyer trust protection structure, as recommended by DingYao. Funds reported as "trust-related capital transfers" with supporting trust documentation. Provides asset isolation and estate planning advantages.

Joint Venture

Multiple investors co-owning property. Each investor's funds must be reported separately, with proportional allocation upon sale. All co-owners must maintain consistent BoP classifications.

Related Non-Property Flows

Foreign buyers frequently move money for reasons other than the property itself. Furniture, fittings and equipment shipped to South Africa are reported under the BOP code for sale of goods, while tuition and living costs for a child at a Cape Town school or university fall under the BOP code for studying, also referred to as the BOP code for education. Mixing these codes with a property transfer is a common and avoidable compliance error.

What Happens If You Use the Wrong BoP Code?

FBPS issues a clear warning: incorrect BoP classification can lead to serious consequences. The most common scenario is delayed fund repatriation — when you sell your property and the bank discovers that the BoP code used for the initial fund entry does not match the exit declaration, the transaction is suspended for review, a process that can take weeks or even months.

In the most severe cases, incorrect codes can result in frozen capital. If the SARB determines that the source or nature of the funds is questionable, it can freeze the relevant capital until the investigation is complete. For buyers who need liquidity or have already planned their next investment, this is a nightmare scenario.

Critical Reminder: The BoP code used must be consistent with the taxpayer's disclosure to the South African Revenue Service (SARS). From a tax compliance perspective, it is very important that your coding matches your tax return, as any inconsistency will raise flags with SARS. This means BoP reporting is not just a banking requirement — it is an integral part of tax compliance.

How Do Foreign Buyers Remit Funds Into South Africa Step by Step?

Short answer: five steps, and the BOP code is only step two. Most failed transfers are not caused by choosing an exotic code — they fail because the payment purpose in the sale agreement, the code on the SWIFT message and the documents attached to the trust account do not tell the same story.

1

Fix the purpose in the sale agreement

The offer to purchase should state that the buyer is a non-resident acquiring South African immovable property. That wording is what your bank uses to select the code.

2

Remit through an Authorised Dealer and declare 510 01

Instruct your bank (an Authorised Dealer) to report the inward payment under 510 01. Where the buyer is a non-resident company or trust, the code is 503.

3

Route the money into the attorney's trust account

South African conveyancing requires purchase funds to enter the transferring attorney's trust account and be released against registration milestones — not paid directly to the seller.

4

Attach the FICA and source-of-funds pack

Identity and address verification, proof of the source of funds, and a tax number where applicable. Limits and documentation thresholds sit with the Authorised Dealer and current SARB rules, not with a fixed number you can assume.

5

Keep the BOP record for the exit

When you later sell and repatriate, the disinvestment leg is reported under the same code family. A complete inward record is what makes the outward leg routine instead of a query.

(Source: SARB Exchange Control / BOP reporting requirements, 2026. Confirm case specifics with your Authorised Dealer.)

How Do You Ensure You Use the Correct BoP Code?

Given South Africa's exchange control framework, foreign real estate investors buying property in the country should ensure the correct BoP classification is used from the outset. Here is a practical guide:

1

Determine Your Investment Structure

Before bringing funds into South Africa, decide on the legal structure for property ownership — individual, company, or trust. Different structures correspond to different BoP classifications.

2

Consult Professional Advisors

Work with advisors familiar with South African exchange control and tax regulations to confirm the applicable BoP code. DingYao can connect you with our partner law firm Garlicke & Bousfield to ensure correct classification from the start.

3

Confirm with Your Bank

Before remitting funds, confirm with your South African commercial bank (such as Standard Bank) that the BoP code being used is correct. As authorised dealers, banks are responsible for ensuring reporting accuracy.

4

Maintain Complete Documentation

Keep all documents related to fund entry, including remittance slips, bank confirmations, and contract documents. These may be required when repatriating funds in the future.

5

Review Compliance Regularly

South Africa's regulatory environment continues to evolve. Periodically review your BoP reporting and tax filing consistency with your advisor to ensure ongoing compliance.

How Will the SARB Update Affect Cape Town's Property Market?

The impact of this BoP code update on Cape Town's property market is two-sided. In the short term, some foreign buyers may delay purchase decisions due to unfamiliarity with the new rules, creating a brief wait-and-see period. However, in the medium to long term, a more precise BoP reporting system will enhance the transparency and efficiency of South Africa's cross-border capital flows, potentially attracting more compliant international capital.

For investors who already hold property in Cape Town, this new regulation means that when selling in the future, the BoP reporting for fund repatriation must match the classification used when funds were originally brought in. If the original reporting had issues, now is the best time to proactively review and correct them.

"If your coding is incorrect, your money will not flow, and if your SARS record is inconsistent with the code used, you face big problems. Getting it right from the start is your best option." — FBPS, Foreign Buyer Property Solutions (15 Jul 2026)

Frequently Asked Questions

What is a BOP code in South Africa?

A BOP code is the Balance of Payments category that an authorised dealer (a commercial bank) must report to the South African Reserve Bank for every cross-border payment. It is written as a three-digit category plus a two-digit sub-code, for example 103 01 for an import payment or 510 01 for a non-resident individual investing in South African property. It records the purpose of the money, not the amount.

Which forex BOP code should a foreign property buyer use in South Africa?

A non-resident individual buying South African property reports under 510 01, the capital-transfer category for investment into property by a non-resident individual. A non-resident company or trust reports under 503 instead. The mirror codes are used on exit: 510 01 and 503 respectively when the property is sold and the proceeds are repatriated.

What is the BOP code for sale of goods in South Africa?

Physical import payments use category 103 with a commodity sub-code (02 capital goods, 03 gold, 04 platinum, 05 crude oil, 06 refined petroleum products, 07 gemstones, 08 steel, 09 coal, 10 iron ore, 11 post); export proceeds use the matching 103 category. Advance payments use 101, 102 or 104. Where goods change hands without any physical shipment, the category is 109, and merchanting transactions are reported under 110.

What is the BOP code for a salary at Standard Bank?

Category 304 covers remuneration paid by a non-resident to a resident employee, and the same category covers a resident employer paying a non-resident employee. Category 303 applies to a resident employee temporarily abroad, 305 to a migrant worker and 306 to a foreign national contract worker. Plain remittances sit under 416 and 417. The code describes the nature of the payment, not which bank receives it.

What happens if the wrong BOP code is used?

The consequences surface at exit. When the property is sold, the bank checks the outward declaration against the inward declaration recorded years earlier; where the two do not reconcile it suspends the transfer for review, which can take weeks or months. In severe cases the SARB can freeze the capital while it investigates the source and nature of the funds.

Do the 2026 BoP changes restrict foreigners from buying South African property?

No. The updated codes do not introduce new restrictions on foreign ownership and do not change the legal rights of non-residents to hold South African property. The change is administrative: it requires more detailed reporting of the funds used to purchase property, mainly so that the original offshore investment is clearly documented when the proceeds are later repatriated.

Why Handle This Through Crestline Advisory?

South African documentation requirements change every year — and what changes is usually the format, not the eligibility. Same passport, same proof of address, wrong format, rejection.

The three most common failure points

  • Passport certification rejected: A plain true-copy stamp is not accepted. A commissioner of oaths must certify in English, confirm the original was seen, add a true-likeness statement for photo pages, and include signature, date, address and occupation.
  • TIN left blank without a reason code: For Taiwanese clients the tax number is the national ID number. Leaving it blank requires ticking Reason A / B / C with an explanation.
  • Proof of address older than three months: Measured from the application date. Past the deadline the entire application is void and must be resubmitted.
